page.layout: One page of running text in one column. In the left margin, beside the lines "rimus. Ad collocatione", there is a marginal note of four short lines.

main_text.p: aliorum quoque bonorum virorum, fimi-li in negotio cùm iudicia, tum fastain me-dium proferenda. Postremò etiam damna atq; pericula recesenda, quę, si contrà quid fiat, metuenda. Nonnunquam & rationes refellendæ sunt, quæ obstare videtur, quo minus nostra locum inuenire consilia possint, eædemq; , aut negandæ: aut eleuandæ atq; extenuandæ: aut aliæ contrariam in parte adferendæ, quæ æquè graues, vel etiam graviores esse videntur. Est verò hîc quoq; opera danda: ne, quæ ad concilian-dum sunt accommodata, omittantur: sed & ἐπαινέσεις[?] collaudationes instituatur ingenij, prudentiæ, doctrinæ, eorum quibus dare consilium volumus: & modesta atq; verecunda nostrarum virium extenuatione arrogantiæ omnis suspicio vitetur: & causæ proponantur breuiter, quib. adduc&ti ad dandū amico consilium impulsi fuerimus. Collocatio sententiarum in singulis suasionum par-tibus[?].Ad collocationē autem quod attinet, quinq; potissimū partib. Suaforię epistolæ absoluuntur, quarum prima Exordiū sententiis maximè ἠθικαῖς[?] & concilian-tib. constat, defumptis, vel ἀ συστάσει[?] laude& commendatione eius ad quę literas damus. lib.2.epist.18.lib.4.epist.7.8. Vel verecunda & modesta nostra extenuatione .lib.4. epist.7.

page.notes: The Greek words are uncertain: ἐπαινέσεις, ἠθικαῖς and συστάσει are read from a small and faint print and are marked [?]. The marginal note's last word, "tibus", is hard to read at the line end. The printed "factain" and "recesenda" look like printing errors and are left as printed. The "&ti" at the start of a line is unclear and may be a printed abbreviation. No catchword or signature is visible.
